citation.title: Medical effectiveness of esophageal balloon pressure manometry in weaning patients from mechanical ventilation

provenance.quote: Patients were included in the study if they received mechanical ventilation for at least 3 days and were able to tolerate intermittent mandatory ventilation with or without pressure support as their primary mode of ventilation.
The medical ICU of Rush-Presbyterian-St. Luke's Medical Center provided all of the patients for this study.

The patient was always weaned by the number of steps allowed by the esophageal weaning protocol. The weaning protocol consisted of a reduction by two, per weaning step, in the number of intermittent mandatory ventilation breaths until a mandatory ventilation rate of 4 breaths/min was achieved, followed by a reduction by 3 cm H2 O of pressure support, per weaning step, until 5 cm H2 O of pressure support was reached.

subgroup_flags.classification_notes: Mixed diagnosis population with 3/23 ARDS. No BMI reported. Balloon placed at study entry after ≥3 days of ventilation; timing relative to intubation/ICU admission not stated beyond that. No transpulmonary pressure target — the balloon data were used for a weaning score, not PEEP titration.

extraction_flags.overlap_evidence: No trial registration reported. Single centre (Rush-Presbyterian-St. Luke's Medical Center, Chicago, 1995 publication) predates and does not match any cluster in COHORTS.md (EPVent, EPVent-2, MGH, Mannheim, Angers). No overlap concluded.
unclear_items: eligibility.criteria.adults_18_plus: no explicit age criterion stated; coded yes from mean age 65.2 yr and adult ICU setting.

intervention.balloon_calibration.method: coded signal_quality_verification_only from 'position verified in the usual manner'; the paper gives no filling volume, occlusion test, or acceptance criterion detail.

design.study_design: coded prospective_cohort with within_patient_crossover comparison; the paper calls itself a 'Prospective study' with each patient as own control, which does not map cleanly onto a single schema design enum.

outcomes: the study's primary contrast is weaning duration, not PEEP titration; recorded under duration_mechanical_ventilation with paired effect, but the study fails the review's balloon_guided_peep_titration criterion and is excluded.
feasibility.n_placement_attempted: the paper does not explicitly state 23 balloons were attempted; inferred from 23 patients entered.
data_only_in_figure: Per-patient weaning times for both protocols (Figure 1, side-by-side bar chart, patients 1-23)
extraction_flags.general_notes: Study uses esophageal balloon data (work of breathing, P0.1, frequency/tidal volume via Bicore CP-100) to guide weaning, not PEEP titration; excluded per COHORTS.md eligibility note. Additional reported results: if the clinician had accelerated weaning on all occasions, duration would have been 7.02 +/- 2.66 days; 65% of clinical evaluations accelerated weaning, overestimated in 4.5%; work of breathing sensitivity 0.95/PPV 0.84, P0.1 sensitivity 0.82/PPV 0.81, frequency/tidal volume sensitivity 0.96/PPV 0.81 in the 56 instances where the esophageal protocol was more aggressive; protocols equally aggressive in 55 instances (39.8%); 11 instances (8.0%) overestimated weaning ability. Table 5 dispersions are SEM per footnote, though the statistics section states 'Data are mean +/- SD'.
